review: 1:1 אֲבִי הָאָב — 'Father of the Father' keeps the Arabic's unusual يا أبا الآب (an Aramaic-style vocative); a smoother 'O Father' would lose the echo of Abba.
2:3 רוּחַ הַבְּנִיּוּת — Romans 8:15 (רוּחַ הַבְּנִיּוּת); the glossary fixes בְּנִיּוּת for the adoption term, and the construct is the New Testament phrase.

3:3–3:4 אַךְ הַחֶסֶד הִרְבָּה / עַל־פֶּשַׁע וְשֶׁחֶת — 'but grace abounded over sin and corruption'; the Arabic زَادَت فَوْقَ is 'increased beyond', and הִרְבָּה is the biblical verb of abundance (1 Sam 1:12).

4:4 כְּדָבָר פִּיךָ הַצַּח — 'according to Your clear word'; צַח is the biblical 'clear/bright' (Song 5:10 of a ruddy complexion is unrelated; Isa 32:4 uses it of clear speech), and it fills the last line.
